rejected.title: Companies
card: Company
A business owned by shareholders. A shareholder owns a share, which is a part of the company. It is also called a corporation.
A company is legally separate from its owners. The law treats it as its own legal person, so it can own property, sign contracts and owe debts in its own name.
Because of this, shareholders can lose only what they put in. If the company fails, their own homes and savings are not used to pay its debts.
A company can have many shareholders, so it can raise money by selling shares. Some companies are small and some are very large.
rejected.remember: A company is its own legal person, so shareholders risk only what they invested.

a.q: Ravi buys shares in a Perth company for $1000. The company later fails with large debts. What is the most Ravi can lose?
opts: The $1000 he put in
All of his savings and his home
Half of the company's debts
The full amount the company owes
a.why: A company is legally separate from its owners, so shareholders lose only what they put in. Ravi's $1000 is at risk, but his own home and savings are not used to pay the company's debts.
a.clue: The company owes the debts, not the shareholders.

b.q: Why can a company sign a contract in its own name, unlike a sole trader's business?
opts: It is legally separate from its shareholders
It has more shareholders than a sole trader has
It always makes more profit than a sole trader
Its shareholders are all personally responsible
b.why: A company is its own legal person, so it can sign contracts and owe debts itself. Having many shareholders is common but is not the reason. The option saying shareholders are personally responsible is wrong, because they can lose only what they put in.
b.clue: Think about who the law treats the company as being.

a.q: Lena paid $500 for shares in a Darwin company. The company closes owing far more than it has. What is the most Lena can lose?
opts: The $500 she paid for her shares
Her savings and her car as well
Her share of all the company's debts
Everything the company still owes
a.why: A company is legally separate from its shareholders, so they lose no more than they put in. Lena's $500 is at risk, but the company's debts are its own, so she does not have to pay a share of them.
a.clue: Whose debts are they, Lena's or the company's?

b.q: A furniture company in Adelaide buys a warehouse and signs a lease on a shop. What allows it to do these things in its own name?
opts: The law treats it as separate from its owners
Its shareholders share all of its debts equally
It has more owners than most small businesses
It sells shares to raise money from investors
b.why: A company is its own legal person, separate from its shareholders, so it can own property and sign contracts itself. Selling shares is a way it can raise money, but that is not what lets it act in its own name.
b.clue: Who does the law see as the owner of the warehouse?

a.best: The $500 she paid for her shares

b.best: The law treats it as separate from its owners
